notes_uk: Also class here: Photographic arts. notes_uk: Тут класифікувати: фоторепортаж, соціальні документальні та вуличні фотографії, фотографії подій та знаменитостей Дивитись також: DNP

DO NOT USE: for traditional Icelandic or Old Norse sagas, See also: FS
notes_uk: Тут класифікувати: сімейні саги. Використовувати для: жанрових романів, які описують життя та долю сім’ї або ряду споріднених чи взаємопов’язаних сімей протягом певного періоду, а часто і протягом поколінь. Часто це серії романів. Використовувати з: FR * кодами для романтичних саг або з кодом FV, коли історична обстановка особливо важлива. НЕ ВИКОРИСТОВУВАТИ: для традиційних ісландських або давньоскандинавських саг Дивитись також: FS

notes_en: Also class here: Comedic stories, comedy fiction, funny and comic novels. Use for: fiction where humour is the primary aim and feature except prefer genre-specific ‘humorous’ headings where available. Use with: other F* codes as appropriate, for humorous genre fiction
notes_uk: Використовувати для: художньої літератури, де гумор є головною метою та особливістю, за винятком тих, які надають перевагу жанровим „жартівливим» заголовкам, якщо такі є. Використовувати з: іншими кодами F * за необхідності

notes_en: Use for: humorous fiction which is satirical and/or which parodies existing fiction, genres or writers, See also: WHP FYH
notes_uk: Використовувати для: гумористичної художньої літератури, яка є сатиричною та / або яка пародіює існуючу художню літературу, жанри чи письменників Дивитись також: WHP FYH

notes_en: Use for: stories set in the past (typically before the writer’s lifetime), where the time period is a significant or essential part of the story and that portray the spirit, manners, and social conditions of that time with realistic detail. Use with: other F* codes as appropriate and PLACE 1* and/or TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers to indicate setting as appropriate. Prefer: genre-specific ‘historical’ headings where available, See also: FFH FJH FMH FRH
notes_uk: Використовувати для: прозових творів, написаних про минуле (як правило, до життя письменника), де часовий проміжок є значною частиною історії, які відображають дух, манери та соціальні умови того часу з реалістичними деталями. Використовувати з: іншими кодами F *, де це необхідно. Використовувати з: визначниками МІСЦЯ 1 * та / або ЧАСОВОГО ПЕРІОДУ 3 * для відображення місця і часу дії сюжету. Віддавати перевагу: специфічним історичним жанровим заголовкам, якщо такі є Дивитись також: FFH FJH FMH FRH

notes_en: Also class here: faith-inspired or inspirational fiction. Use for: fiction designed to promote a particular religious, spiritual or visionary message. Use with: 5PG* values from INTEREST 5* Qualifiers as appropriate, or where unavailable, a QR* or VX* code and with other F* codes, for example FR* for Religious romance novels, with VX* codes for visionary or spiritual fiction, with 5PGM for Christian Fiction, etc
notes_uk: Використовувати для: художньої літератури, призначеної для пропагування певного релігійного, духовного чи містичного послання. Використовувати із: визначниками 5PG *з ІНТЕРЕС 5 *, якщо це необхідно або там, де неможливо застосувати коди QR * або VX *. Використовувати з: іншими кодами F *, наприклад FR * для релігійних любовних романів

description_en: Fiction / Literature / Comics / Graphic novels: narrative themes
notes_en: Use all FX* codes for: identifying the primary theme of a narrative work, when that theme is not conveyed by the choice of a genre fiction or manga, comic book or graphic novel category. Use all FX* codes with: FB* codes or other F* codes indicating genre or type, or with Literature DB*, DC*, DD* or Comics (Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga etc): genre XQ* codes, to indicate the principal underlying narrative theme of a work of fiction, literature, poetry, drama theatre, comic books etc. FX* codes can also be used in conjunction with non-fiction categories to give greater definition to the narrative theme where appropriate, FX itself can be used with a non-fiction code if there is not a suitable other FX* code. DO NOT USE: FX* codes as the primary or main subject code or simply to indicate a mood or emotion evoked by a story
notes_uk: Використовувати всі коди FX * для: визначення основної теми художньої прози, коли ця тема не передається вибором категорії жанрової літератури. Використовувати всі коди FX * з: іншими кодами F *, що вказують на жанр чи тип, або кодами DB *, DC *, DD * і XQ * для відображення основної теми розповіді художнього твору. Коди FX * можуть також використовуватися разом із нехудожніми категоріями, щоб чіткіше відобразити сюжет. НЕ ВИКОРИСТОВУВАТИ: FX * коди як основний предметний код

notes_en: Also class here: bildungsroman, growing up, rites of passage, passage from childhood or youth to adulthood as narrative themes, stories about a young person going from being a child to being an adult
notes_uk: Тут класифікувати: білдунгсроман ( жанр роману, який показує подорож молодого героя від дитинства до дорослості ,або незрілості до зрілості, з акцентом на випробуваннях і нещастях, що впливають на ріст персонажа)

description_en: Narrative theme: books and the world of books
description_uk: Narrative theme: books and the world of books
notes_en: Also class here: stories, novels and works of fiction where the main theme is about the world of books, including, booksellers, bookshops, libraries, literature, writers, the art of writing, books about reading, books about books, book clubs, publishers or any story that has a main theme taken from the world of books
notes_uk: Also class here: stories, novels and works of fiction where the main theme is about the world of books, including, booksellers, bookshops, libraries, literature, writers, the art of writing, books about reading, books about books, book clubs, publishers or any story that has a main theme taken from the world of books

notes_en: Use for: fiction where a strong relationship or love is the central theme but which is not a genre romance novel. This can include friendships, found family, family relationships, sibling relationships, parent-child relationships, any form of affective relationship, relationships between couples, relationships that are negative or hostile, or complex emotional relationships, forbidden love, a love triangle, unrequited love, love of family, relationships amongst a group of friends or a peer group, examination of relationships with others, acquaintances, strangers etc, as long as it is one of the principal themes of the story. Use with: INTEREST 5* Qualifiers for detail of specific kinds of relationships as appropriate. DO NOT USE: with FR* codes
notes_uk: Використовуйте для: нежанрової любовної художньої літератури, де міцні стосунки чи кохання є центральною темою. Це може включати дружбу, сімейні стосунки тощо, якщо це одна з основних тем історії. Використовувати з: визначниками ІНТЕРЕС 5 * для деталізації конкретних видів стосунків за необхідності

description_en: Narrative theme: environmental issues / the natural world
notes_en: Use for: fiction that addresses a specific environmental issue or nature-orientated topics as a central theme. Use with: other subject codes to give more specific definition to the topic if appropriate, for example, FD*, FL* , FF* or FH* codes for Climate fiction (Cli-fi), Eco-fiction or eco-thrillers or FB* for nature writing in fiction, or with XQ* codes for comic books, graphic novels or manga that have major themes around the natural world or the environment
notes_uk: Використовуйте для: художньої літератури, яка вирішує певну екологічну проблему як центральну тему

notes_en: Use for: fiction or stories that feature animals or any living creature as a major or significant part of the plot or theme, or where human interactions or relationships with animals, including pets, is a main part of the plot, or one or more of the main characters or protagonists are animals. Use with: WN* codes if the story is about a specific type of animal, for example, WNGC for stories about cats, or WNGD for stories about dogs
notes_uk: Use for: fiction or stories that feature animals or any living creature as a major or significant part of the plot or theme, or where human interactions or relationships with animals, including pets, is a main part of the plot, or one or more of the main characters or protagonists are animals. Use with: WN* codes if the story is about a specific type of animal, for example, WNGC for stories about cats, or WNGD for stories about dogs

notes_en: Use for: works of fiction that take place during periods of war or armed conflict or civil strife, and where the experience or consequences of war, or battle or armed conflict is the major theme or topic of the story and is explored through the plot or the development of the main characters. Prefer: FJM* codes for action and adventure war fiction, See also: FJM*
notes_uk: Use for: works of fiction that take place during periods of war or armed conflict or civil strife, and where the experience or consequences of war, or battle or armed conflict is the major theme or topic of the story and is explored through the plot or the development of the main characters. Prefer: FJM* codes for action and adventure war fiction Дивитись також: FJM*

notes_en: Use for: fiction where health, coping or living with illness – physical or mental – or the consequences of sickness is a central theme, or themes based on medical topics or suffering linked to physical or mental health, chronic illness or conditions, chronic pain, or themes around the healing, recovery or recuperation from illness
notes_uk: Use for: fiction where health, coping or living with illness – physical or mental – or the consequences of sickness is a central theme, or themes based on medical topics or suffering linked to physical or mental health, chronic illness or conditions, chronic pain, or themes around the healing, recovery or recuperation from illness

notes_en: Use for: fiction where death, dying, the end-of-life, a loss or the experience of grief or mourning is a central theme and one of the key elements of the story, but not for genre fiction like crime, thriller or adventure novels that happen to have a death in them
notes_uk: Використовуйте для: художньої літератури, де втрата або переживання горя є центральною темою

description_en: Narrative theme: interior life / psychological fiction
notes_en: Also class here: psychological realism, character-driven psychological stories, stories with an interior monologue or stream of consciousness. Use for: fiction which places particular emphasis on interior characterization, and on the motives, emotions, feelings and thoughts or mental lives of characters, stories that explore the mental state of a character. Prefer: FHX for psychological thrillers, See also: FHX
notes_uk: Використовувати для: художньої літератури, яка робить особливий акцент на характеристиці інтер’єру, а також на мотивах, почуттях і думках персонажів. Віддавати перевагу: FHX для психологічних трилерів Дивитись також: FHX

notes_en: Use for: fiction where the identity, the sense of, or search for, identity of whatever kind – social, cultural, religious, gender etc, as an individual or part of a group – of the main character(s) is the main, or one of the main themes of the story, or narratives where the characters sense of belonging or search or need for belonging is the main or major theme of the plot. Use with: other subject codes and INTEREST 5* Qualifiers as appropriate
notes_uk: Використовувати для: художньої літератури, де ідентичність, відчуття або пошук особистості (будь-якої, соціальної, культурної, релігійної, гендерної та ін.) головних персонажів є основною або однією з основних тем. Використовувати з: іншими тематичними кодами та визначниками ІНТЕРЕС 5 * за необхідності

notes_en: Also class here: Political novels, fiction as political or economic criticism, novels of political satire, fiction as commentary or discussion on politics, economics, society, government, diplomacy, politicians or political culture, political power, political corruption as major themes of a story. Use for: fiction or literature where political or economic concerns are the underlying narrative theme including political or economic allegories. Use with: DC* for political poetry. Prefer: FHP for political thrillers, See also: FHP
notes_uk: Використовувати для: художньої літератури, де політичні проблеми є основною темою розповіді, включаючи політичні алегорії. Віддавати перевагу: FHP для політичних трилерів Дивитись також: FHP

notes_en: Use for: fiction that has major themes relating to diasporas, dispersion, asylum, deracination, forced relocation, cultural transitions, forced journeys, living in exile, being exiled, emigration, expatriation, immigration, refugees, forced resettlement, etc, See also: FXV
notes_uk: Використовувати для: художньої літератури, яка має основні теми, що стосуються діаспор, розпорошення, притулку, деракації, примусового переселення, культурних переходів, примусових подорожей тощо Дивитись також: FXV

notes_en: Use for: fiction set in a real location where the setting or landscape very deeply pervades the work to the extent that it could not be set anywhere else; e.g. the French tradition of ‘roman du terroir’. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers, and other subject codes for example, with JBSD for novels where city life is a main theme, or JBSG for reservation life or rez lit, or JBSE for small town life novels, JBSC for works of fiction where the setting in a small town, village, a rural area, or in the countryside and the associated lifestyle or living conditions are critical to the sense and meaning of the story
notes_uk: Використовувати для: художньої літератури, розміщеної в реальному місці (часто, але не обов’язково в сільській чи історичній місцевості), де декорація дуже глибоко пронизує твір до такої міри, що його дія не могла відбуватись в іншому місці; напр. французька традиція «римський дю теруар». Використовувати з: визначниками МІСЦЯ 1 *

description_en: Narrative theme: social issues / social problems
notes_en: Also class here: Social protest novels, fiction as social commentary, stories about social unrest. Use for: fiction that addresses a specific social problem or issue as a central theme, such as, poverty or precarity, economic inequalities, homelessness, housing issues, conditions in factories and mines, the plight of child labour, violence against women, rising criminality, and epidemics because of over-crowding and poor sanitation in cities or works of fiction in which a prevailing social problem, such as gender, race, or class prejudice, is dramatized through its effect on the characters of a novel. Use with: other non-fiction codes, especially JBF* codes, to give more detail of the main social issue but an F* code MUST be designated as the Main Subject
notes_uk: Використовувати для: художньої літератури, яка вирішує певну соціальну проблему чи питання як центральну тему. Використовувати разом із: іншими нехудожніми кодами, особливо кодами JBF * деталізації основної соціальної проблеми

description_en: Narrative theme: diversity, equity, equality, inclusion
description_uk: Narrative theme: diversity, equity, equality, inclusion
notes_en: Use for: works of fiction where the main narrative theme or subject matter clearly illustrates topics relating to aspects of accessibility, social justice, equity or equality, diversity and inclusivity within the context of the story, or the story explores themes of DEI, or attempts to achieve DEI. Use with: other subject codes and INTEREST 5* Qualifiers to give greater detail as appropriate
notes_uk: Use for: works of fiction where the main narrative theme or subject matter clearly illustrates topics relating to aspects of accessibility, social justice, equity or equality, diversity and inclusivity within the context of the story, or the story explores themes of DEI, or attempts to achieve DEI. Use with: other subject codes and INTEREST 5* Qualifiers to give greater detail as appropriate

notes_en: Also class here: road trip stories, stories about voyages of exploration and discovery, stories about quests, epic journeys or about wanderers. Use for: fiction where a journey, expedition, voyage or some sort of travel or trip is the main or a major narrative theme of the story, See also: FXQ
notes_uk: Also class here: road trip stories, stories about voyages of exploration and discovery, stories about quests, epic journeys or about wanderers. Use for: fiction where a journey, expedition, voyage or some sort of travel or trip is the main or a major narrative theme of the story Дивитись також: FXQ

description_en: Fiction / Literature / Comics / Graphic novels: special features
notes_en: Use all FY* codes with: other F* code indicating genre or subject, or with literature DB*, DC*, DD* or Comics (Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga etc), genre XQ* codes, to indicate the principal underlying distinct aspects, attributes, characteristic or features of a work of fiction. FY* codes should not usually be the primary or main subject code. DO NOT USE: FY itself - always use FY* codes
notes_uk: Використовувати всі коди FY * з: іншим кодом F * для відображення жанру або типу. Коди FY *, як правило, не повинні бути основними або основними предметними

notes_en: Also class here: Anthologies or collections of short works of fiction either by the same author or by multiple authors. Use with: DNT for anthologies of short stories by theme or by multiple authors
notes_uk: Also class here: Anthologies or collections of short works of fiction either by the same author or by multiple authors. Use with: DNT for anthologies of short stories by theme or by multiple authors

notes_en: Use for: works of fiction that are neither seen as short stories nor as novels by their creators
notes_uk: Use for: works of fiction that are neither seen as short stories nor as novels by their creators

notes_en: Use for: fiction, literature, comic books or any fictional narratives that are written in a series of documents, letters, diaries, journals, emails, blogs, social media posts, etc
notes_uk: Використовувати для: художньої літератури, написаної в серії документів, листів, щоденників, електронних листів, блогів тощо

notes_en: Also class here: Continuation novels. Use for: works of fiction where a new author continues an established series after the original authors death. These can be official with the permission of the literary estate or unofficial for works now out of copyright. These stories may be sequels to the original series or be stories that are prequels or precede the original storyline, but all the stories are written after the original authors death
notes_uk: Also class here: Continuation novels. Use for: works of fiction where a new author continues an established series after the original authors death. These can be official with the permission of the literary estate or unofficial for works now out of copyright. These stories may be sequels to the original series or be stories that are prequels or precede the original storyline, but all the stories are written after the original authors death

notes_en: Use for: fiction written deliberately in the style of another (typically earlier) author (as homage rather than parody), See also: FUP
notes_uk: Використовувати для: художньої літератури, написаної у стилі іншого автора (як пошана, а не пародія), часто як продовження роману, написаного оригінальним автором або з використанням популярного персонажа Дивитись також: FUP

notes_en: Also class here: Past-Present narratives. Use for: fiction, literature, comic books or any fictional narratives that have storylines featuring two or more timelines (but where there is no time travelling or time slips), where a single cohesive narrative, is told using multiple time periods and perspectives
notes_uk: Also class here: Past-Present narratives. Use for: fiction, literature, comic books or any fictional narratives that have storylines featuring two or more timelines (but where there is no time travelling or time slips), where a single cohesive narrative, is told using multiple time periods and perspectives

notes_en: Use for: fiction, literature, comic books or any fictional narratives that are usually create an atmosphere of tension and suspense for the reader using psychological techniques and often feature themes things like a sense of fear and haunting, gloom or death, a dark past, a claustrophobic atmosphere, an oppressive, bleak, decayed or derelict setting, the threat of supernatural events, and the intrusion of the past upon the present and that often inspire fear through a romanticized view of the past, and often combining elements of both horror and romance etc. Use with: FR* for Gothic romance, FK* for Gothic horror, other F* codes for other types of Gothic fiction, with PLACE1* Qualifiers for gothic fiction associated with a particular area, such as 1KBB-US-S* codes - for Southern Gothic (USA) or 1KL* codes for gothic fiction set in Latin America
notes_uk: Use for: fiction, literature, comic books or any fictional narratives that are usually create an atmosphere of tension and suspense for the reader using psychological techniques and often feature themes things like a sense of fear and haunting, gloom or death, a dark past, a claustrophobic atmosphere, an oppressive, bleak, decayed or derelict setting, the threat of supernatural events, and the intrusion of the past upon the present and that often inspire fear through a romanticized view of the past, and often combining elements of both horror and romance etc. Use with: FR* for Gothic romance, FK* for Gothic horror, other F* codes for other types of Gothic fiction, with PLACE1* Qualifiers for gothic fiction associated with a particular area, such as 1KBB-US-S* codes - for Southern Gothic (USA) or 1KL* codes for gothic fiction set in Latin America

notes_en: Also class here: mash-up or mashed-up novels. Use for: fiction which combines a pre-existing text, often a classic novel, with another contrasting genre, such as horror, into a single narrative, or that takes fictional characters, settings, or universes from different fictions and places them into a single story. Use with: other F* or non-fiction codes to indicate component elements, See also: FUP
notes_uk: Also class here: mash-up or mashed-up novels. Use for: fiction which combines a pre-existing text, often a classic novel, with another contrasting genre, such as horror, into a single narrative, or that takes fictional characters, settings, or universes from different fictions and places them into a single story. Use with: other F* or non-fiction codes to indicate component elements Дивитись також: FUP

description_en: Fiction based on or inspired by true events
description_uk: Fiction based on or inspired by true events
notes_en: Use for: fiction based on or inspired by a true event or happening but where this is told in narrative fictionalised form and is not just an account of the event itself. Use with: other F* codes to describe the genre or with Literature DB*, DC*, DD*, comic books XQ* codes. Prefer: DNX for narrative accounts of true stories, or FC for fiction based on peoples lives, See also: DNX FC
notes_uk: Use for: fiction based on or inspired by a true event or happening but where this is told in narrative fictionalised form and is not just an account of the event itself. Use with: other F* codes to describe the genre or with Literature DB*, DC*, DD*, comic books XQ* codes. Prefer: DNX for narrative accounts of true stories, or FC for fiction based on peoples lives Дивитись також: DNX FC

description_en: Fiction: special features: yaoi / BL / danmei novels
notes_en: Also class here: boys’ love novels. Use for: East Asian style stories, often related to comics or anime, featuring male same-sex relationships, created principally, but not exclusively, for a female readership. Use with: other F* codes to indicate genre, for example FR* codes for Romance stories, 5LKE * codes if they are about that generation, See also: XAMT
notes_uk: Also class here: boys’ love novels. Use for: East Asian style stories, often related to comics or anime, featuring male same-sex relationships, created principally, but not exclusively, for a female readership. Use with: other F* codes to indicate genre, for example FR* codes for Romance stories, 5LKE * codes if they are about that generation Дивитись також: XAMT

notes_en: Use for: the kind of romance, science fiction or other types of genre fiction or comic books, usually published on a monthly basis, short, in clearly delineated lines and with a certain number published every month. Use with: other F* code indicating genre or type, for example, with FR*codes for Category or Series Romance. DO NOT USE: FYR as the main or primary subject or the only code
notes_uk: Use for: the kind of romance, science fiction or other types of genre fiction or comic books, usually published on a monthly basis, short, in clearly delineated lines and with a certain number published every month. Use with: other F* code indicating genre or type, for example, with FR*codes for Category or Series Romance. DO NOT USE: FYR as the main or primary subject or the only code

notes_en: Also class here: Raito noberu, Japanese novellas, illustrated novellas. Use for: short fiction aimed at adults, usually driven primarily by dialogue and character and generally accompanied by illustrations in manga/anime or similar styles. Use with: other F* codes to indicate the genre. FYS may be used as a main subject as appropriate
notes_uk: Also class here: Raito noberu, Japanese novellas, illustrated novellas. Use for: short fiction aimed at adults, usually driven primarily by dialogue and character and generally accompanied by illustrations in manga/anime or similar styles. Use with: other F* codes to indicate the genre. FYS may be used as a main subject as appropriate

notes_en: Use for: fiction and literature translated from another language. Use with: F* or with Literature DB*, DC*, DD*, or comic book XQ* codes to ensure classification is meaningful beyond the translation of the work itself and with 5T* - Literature of Place Qualifiers as appropriate. DO NOT USE: PLACE 1* or LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers to specify the original language (this is described in other metadata). You may still use a PLACE 1* Qualifier if it is relevant to the plot or setting of the book. DO NOT USE: FYT as the main or primary subject or the only code
notes_uk: Use for: fiction and literature translated from another language. Use with: F* or with Literature DB*, DC*, DD*, or comic book XQ* codes to ensure classification is meaningful beyond the translation of the work itself and with 5T* - Literature of Place Qualifiers as appropriate. DO NOT USE: PLACE 1* or LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers to specify the original language (this is described in other metadata). You may still use a PLACE 1* Qualifier if it is relevant to the plot or setting of the book. DO NOT USE: FYT as the main or primary subject or the only code

description_en: Fiction: inspired by or adapted from other media
notes_en: Use for: stories that were published as spin-offs or companions to pre-existing non-book media or merchandise, novelizations and novels inspired by a popular film franchise, an online game or a TV series. Use with: other F* codes indicating genre or type, or with Literature DB*, DC*, DD* codes if this work is presented as a poem or a play, or XQ* for comic book. notes_en: Use PLACE 1* Qualifier codes WITH appropriate subject codes for: indicating the geographical scope and applicability of the content, such as the location of a travel guide, the setting of a novel, the jurisdiction to which laws apply, the history of a particular place, the peoples, arts, traditions, or culture of a particular geographical location, etc. Where options exist, e.g. terms representing actual, historical, cultural, administrative, or geophysical entities, use the expression that best suits the content. Where no code exists for a specific location, use the nearest most appropriate broader code that includes it. DO NOT USE: to indicate any geographical aspect that is not to do with the content or subject of a book (e.g. place of publication, market availability, nationality of author – this is described in other metadata, etc). National extensions (i.e. 1*-xx- format codes, where ‘xx’ indicates a country code) can be assigned by any user, and are not exclusive to users in the indicated country. This section is not intended as an exhaustive gazetteer of all places but a list of commonly used locations in the global book supply chain. notes_uk: Використовуйте PLACE 1 * Кваліфікаційні коди З відповідними кодами предметів для: вказівки географічного обсягу та застосовності вмісту, таких як місцезнаходження туристичного путівника, постановка роману, юрисдикція, до якої застосовуються закони, історія певного місця і т. д. Там, де існують варіанти, наприклад терміни, що представляють фактичні, історичні, культурні, адміністративні чи геофізичні утворення, використовуйте вираз, який найкраще відповідає змісту. Якщо для певного місця не існує коду, використовуйте найближчий найбільш підходящий ширший код, який його включає. НЕ ВИКОРИСТОВУЙТЕ: для позначення будь-якого географічного аспекту, який не пов’язаний із змістом або темою книги (наприклад, місце видання, наявність на ринку, національність автора - це описано в інших метаданих тощо). Національні розширення (тобто коди формату 1 * -xx-, де ‘xx’ вказує код країни) може бути призначений будь-яким користувачем і не є виключним для користувачів у зазначеній країні. Цей розділ призначений не як вичерпний вісник усіх місць, а як перелік загальновживаних місць у світовому ланцюжку поставок книг. НЕ ВИКОРИСТОВУЙТЕ: сам код «1», але виберіть відповідні конкретні кваліфікатори з розділу 1 *

notes_en: Use all 5A* age codes for: defining the Y* or X* codes – 5A* age numbers are used instead of named codes, such as juvenile, middle grade, young adult, as these have different meanings in different countries or languages. Select one 5A* code indicating a general guideline starting or base interest age of the content in any works aimed primarily at children or teenagers. All Y* codes (except YP* which use 4* codes) MUST be accompanied by one 5A* qualifier code to give guidance of interest age, for example: book content for an audience of 9 to 12 age group, should use 5AK, as the lower age; content of interest to teenagers should use 5AP or 5AQ; content for older teenagers and young adults should use 5AS, 5AT or 5AU as appropriate. 5AR, 5AX and 5AZ can be used with any relevant subject code. All 5A* codes can be used with X* subject codes if the Comic book is aimed at children or teenagers. DO NOT USE: 5A itself – always use 5A* codes.
